title: Classification or Regression?
outcome: By the end, I can explain classification or regression? using a traced example and a stated limitation.
scenario: Distinguish predicting growth height from predicting a growth category.
given: Actual heights are [4, 7, 9] cm; estimates are [5, 6, 10] cm. Tall means strictly greater than 6 cm.
All inputs and outcomes in this worked example are invented classroom data; no real model run is claimed.

steps.label: Regression errors
steps.detail: Absolute errors are 1, 1, 1 cm; mean absolute error is 1 cm.

steps.label: Actual categories
steps.detail: Actual classes are short, tall, tall.

steps.label: Predicted categories
steps.detail: Estimated classes are short, short, tall: 2/3 correct.

explanation: Read the picture in order. Estimated classes are short, short, tall: 2/3 correct. The arrows show which recorded input or intermediate result each decision uses. Explain the deciding step aloud before checking the changed case; pointing to the final answer alone does not show how it follows.

counterfactual.change: Change the category boundary to strictly greater than 7 cm.
counterfactual.prediction: Actual and estimated categories both become short, short, tall: 3/3 correct.
counterfactual.reason: The numerical estimates did not improve; the decision definition changed.

student_task: Did regression MAE improve when the boundary changed? Point to the relevant step in the picture, then write the changed result and the rule or evidence that supports it.
teacher_answer: No. MAE remains 1 cm. Category agreement rose because the class boundary changed, not because predictions became numerically closer. Changed-case check: Actual and estimated categories both become short, short, tall: 3/3 correct. The numerical estimates did not improve; the decision definition changed.
project_evidence: For your Responsible Plant Classifier, save the input, procedure, observed result and limitation of this check. Label this worked example as practice; use a different, previously unreviewed case when checking independent understanding.
limits: Regression error and category accuracy measure different targets; neither alone covers every use consequence.
review_note: Reviewed Classification or Regression? against the assigned lesson pack and its reserved independent case. Added a different explicit worked scenario, an auditable trace and a changed-input check; preserved the original curriculum and assessment boundary.
